suggestions: Collapse the up-minus-down correlation split into a single signed rolling correlation: replace the two masked Corr(...,20) terms with one Corr(Sign((close-open)/open)*(((close-open)/open)-((open-Delay(close,1))/Delay(close,1))), Sign((close-open)/open)*Diff(Log(close*volume),1), 20) (optionally wrapped in Tanh). Investment rationale: gating to small-gap days already cuts the sample roughly in half; splitting that subset again by intraday direction leaves each 20-day window with too few non-zero points for stable Pearson estimates, which explains the collapse from parent RankIC≈0.04 to near zero—sign-weighting encodes the same directional liquidity asymmetry (volume should co-move with session efficiency on up days and not on down days) in one estimator with full effective sample size.

Replace the hard gap-regime zero mask Less(Abs((open-Delay(close,1))/Delay(close,1)), Med(Abs((open-Delay(close,1))/Delay(close,1)), 20)) with a continuous session-discovery weight, e.g. Exp(-Abs((open-Delay(close,1))/Delay(close,1))/Med(Abs((open-Delay(close,1))/Delay(close,1)), 20)), applied to both legs before correlation (or as a weighted correlation). Investment rationale: the binary gate drives coverage to ~45% and discards marginal small/medium-gap days that still contain usable price–volume information; a smooth down-weight of large overnight jumps preserves the economic focus on intraday price discovery while retaining enough daily observations for correlation estimates to converge and RankIC to recover.

Stabilize the dollar-flow input and lengthen the estimation window: swap Diff(Log(close*volume),1) for Ma(Diff(Log(close*volume),1), 5) and extend the correlation window from 20 to 40–60 days on the unified signed structure above. Investment rationale: one-day log dollar-flow changes are dominated by microstructure noise and event spikes that inflate in-sample correlation but fail forward (consistent with rank_ic_valid < 0); institutional funded-demand confirmation is a slower process, so a smoothed dollar-acceleration leg paired with a longer rolling window targets the persistent co-movement that actually predicts next-period returns rather than transient liquidity bursts.
